content.text:
Catalog search results now sort the way librarians file them, ignoring a leading "The", "A" or "An", so "The Hobbit" lands under H. All 60 tests pass.

- **`lib/helpers/text.js`:** I added `filingTitle(title)`, which strips one leading article. It matches whole words only, so "Anathem" keeps its "An". A title that is only an article, like "The", is left as it is.
- **`lib/catalog/search.js`:** `searchCatalog` sorts on `filingTitle`. Two titles that file the same way, such as "The Hobbit" and "Hobbit", fall back to the full title.
- **`test/catalog.test.js`:** I updated the existing sort test, because "The Left Hand of Darkness" now sorts before "National Geographic". I also added a test covering "The", "A" and "An", "Anathem", and a lone "The".

The displayed title is unchanged, and `GET /catalog` picks up the new order automatically. Other sorts, such as the holds queue, overdue list and CSV export, don't sort by title, so I left them alone.

I didn't touch leading punctuation or quotes (for example `"Hamlet"`), since you only asked about the three articles.
